d: The LHSAA has now posted both games. It will be dry and cold, with temperatures dropping toward the low 40s. Two wins from here is the Superdome.
b:

t: Pecan Island and Downtown Abbeville Named Federal Opportunity Zones, Opening Tax Breaks for Investors
d: Two Vermilion Parish areas made the state’s new list. One covers the whole coast, including Pecan Island, where SpaceX plans to build. The breaks start Jan. 1.
b:
Two parts of Vermilion Parish are on Louisiana’s new list of federal Opportunity Zones, places where investors can get tax breaks for putting money into businesses and property. 
 One of them takes in the entire coast of the parish, including Pecan Island, where SpaceX plans to start building in 2027. The other is the middle of Abbeville. 
 The state announced 156 zones on Nov. 13 but did not list them by town. The Vermilion Times pulled the list from the state’s own map and checked the boundaries. 
 The two zones here 
   The coast (Census Tract 9511).  It stretches across the south end of the parish along the Gulf. Pecan Island, Forked Island, Esther, Mouton Cove, Intracoastal City and Freshwater City are all inside it.   Central Abbeville (Census Tract 9507).  A small area, about two miles across, that includes the courthouse square downtown.  
 Kaplan, Gueydan, Erath, Delcambre and Maurice are not in a zone. 
 Both Vermilion zones are classed as rural, which matters: the state says the renewed program gives extra incentives for investments in rural zones. 
 What an Opportunity Zone is 
 It is a federal tax break for investors. Someone who has made a profit selling stock, land or a business can put that money into a project inside a zone, through what the law calls a Qualified Opportunity Fund, and pay less federal tax on it. 
 The state lists these benefits starting Jan. 1, 2027: 
  Tax on the original profit is put off.  The taxable amount is cut by 10%.  Growth in the new investment can be tax-free.  Rural zones get a bigger incentive and easier rules for fixing up property.  
 The Treasury Department says the new zones last 10 years. 
 What it is not 
 It is not a grant, and it does not pay residents or the parish anything directly. It does not change local property taxes. The idea is to make it cheaper for private money to build things in these places: housing, shops, hotels, industrial sites. 
 Whether that happens is up to investors. The designation only makes the area eligible. 
 The bigger picture 
   Statewide:  156 zones, 82 of them rural. Louisiana nominated the most it was allowed to, and all were approved, the state said.   Acadiana:  22 zones. Lafayette Parish has nine, St. Landry four, and Vermilion, Iberia, Acadia and St. Martin two each. Evangeline has one.   Who picked them:  The state says it worked through regional economic development groups, with input from local officials, business leaders and developers.  
 The coast zone lands as SpaceX prepares a launch site the company says will bring more than 3,000 jobs. [SpaceX is taking resumes now, and local businesses can sign up as suppliers.](/news/spacex-taking-resumes-starbase-louisiana-email-supplier-signup/) 
  How we checked:  We downloaded the 156 tracts from the state’s Opportunity Zone map, found the two in Vermilion Parish and tested the location of each town against the tract boundaries.

t: Jensen Huang Gets His Job Back: Nvidia’s Board Reinstates Its CEO 11 Days After He Resigned
d: The board says it heard from “senior levels” of the U.S. government and is confident his return is no national security risk. An investigation into a foreign intelligence effort aimed at him is still open.
b:
Jensen Huang is running Nvidia again. 
 The company’s board voted unanimously Monday to put him back as president and chief executive and to return him to his board seat, effective immediately. He had resigned from all three on Nov. 12. 
 Nvidia makes the computer chips behind much of the artificial intelligence boom. Huang co-founded the company and led it for 33 years. 
 What the board said 
 The board said it reached the decision after “a series of discussions and meetings” with Huang and was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead.” 
 It also said this: the board “received input from senior levels of the United States government,” and based on that, it is “confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” 
 “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said in the company’s announcement. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” 
 How it got here 
 All of this is from Nvidia’s own announcements: 
   Nov. 8:  The board opens an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” It says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.   Nov. 10:  The independent directors hire a former acting U.S. attorney, Joon H. Kim, and his law firm to run the investigation.   Nov. 12:  Huang resigns. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO, and the board says it will search for a permanent replacement.   Nov. 17:  The board creates a committee to oversee national security and export rules.   Nov. 23:  The board reinstates Huang.  
 Nvidia’s statements do not describe the intelligence effort. NBC News, citing earlier reports by The New York Times and the Financial Times, said the reporting concerned Huang’s relationship with a woman whom American intelligence officials suspected of spying for China. 
 The president’s part 
 Nvidia did not say who in the government it heard from. 
 NBC News reported that President Donald Trump said in a television interview that he personally stepped in, speaking “directly and indirectly” with the board. NBC also reported that Trump wrote on social media that the government had “no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a national security risk, and that the attorney general had confirmed the government has no evidence Huang did anything unlawful. 
 Not everyone accepted that. NBC quoted Sen. John Cornyn, a Texas Republican on the Senate Intelligence Committee, as writing: “No national security risk? Based on what?” 
 Nvidia’s stock rose 31% Monday, NBC reported. 
 What is not over 
   The investigation continues.  The board said the independent committee’s work “will proceed to conclusion” and that Huang supports it and will cooperate.   New watchdogs.  Nvidia is hiring a chief compliance officer, a new position, and the board’s national security committee is bringing in outside experts.   Congress.  NBC reported that Huang is still scheduled for a closed-door interview with three House committees on Dec. 1 and a public Senate hearing later that week.   Government inquiries.  Nvidia said it “will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.”  
 Kress goes back to being chief financial officer. Harvey Jones stays on as board chair.

t: Louisiana Is Putting Up Billboards in Houston: ‘It’s Time to Come Home’
d: The state is going after Louisiana natives working in Texas, and Texas companies too. It says nearly 60,000 new jobs have been announced here since 2024.
b:
If you have family who moved to Houston for work, the state of Louisiana is about to ask them to move back. 
 Louisiana Economic Development says it will put up billboards along Interstate 10 East in Houston over the next several weeks. The message is aimed at Louisiana natives living in Texas: “It’s time to come home.” 
 What the state is doing 
   Billboards  on I-10 East in Houston.   A full-page ad  in the Houston Business Journal, aimed at company owners and executives.   A job site.  The campaign sends job seekers to LouisianaNOW.jobs, the state’s free job board.  
 The state calls this the first phase of a larger push into Texas to bring workers back, recruit new companies and compete for investment. 
 Why now 
 The state’s announcement ties the timing to recent elections in Texas, which it says brought “a significant shift in the state’s political leadership.” 
 “Texas, Louisiana is open for business. Come grow with us,” Gov. Jeff Landry said in the announcement. 
 The state says nearly 60,000 new jobs have been announced across Louisiana since 2024. Those are jobs companies have promised, not jobs already filled. 
 What it looks like from here 
 Federal numbers show the work is already picking up. Louisiana added 17,600 construction jobs in the past year, the fastest growth of any state. [We reported that Sunday.](/news/louisiana-adding-construction-jobs-faster-than-any-state/) 
 We also searched the state’s job site Monday for towns in and around Vermilion Parish. [Here are 10 trade jobs it listed](/news/trade-jobs-near-vermilion-parish-welders-dump-truck-abbeville/), including one in Abbeville. 
 SpaceX, which plans to start building at Pecan Island in 2027, is [taking resumes by email now](/news/spacex-taking-resumes-starbase-louisiana-email-supplier-signup/). 
  Know somebody in Texas who wants to come home?  Send them the links above.

t: SpaceX Is Taking Resumes for Starbase Louisiana Now. Here’s the Email, and How Local Businesses Sign Up for the Work
d: The company says it will hire “heavily from nearby communities.” Its Louisiana page has a resume button, and there are two free sign-ups for contractors and suppliers.
b:
You do not have to wait for a job posting to get your name in front of SpaceX. 
 The company’s own page for Starbase, Louisiana, has a “Submit a Resume” button. It opens an email to a hiring address set up for the Louisiana site. 
 If you want a job 
  Email your resume to starbaselajobs@spacex.com.  
 That is the address behind the button on SpaceX’s Starbase, LA page. The button fills in the subject line “Joining the Starbase, LA team” and a short note saying you are sending a resume and an introduction. 
 On the same page, SpaceX says it is committed to “creating more than 3,000 new jobs” at the site, “hiring heavily from nearby communities” and using Louisiana workers’ experience building complex projects in this environment. 
 What the page does not say: which jobs the resumes are for, what they pay, or when hiring will start. SpaceX lists construction as starting in 2027 and the first Starship launch in 2029. 
 Jobs with full descriptions are posted on a separate careers board. There were 12 for Pecan Island as of this morning, the same 12 as Saturday. [Here is every one and how to apply.](/news/every-spacex-job-open-pecan-island-12-positions-how-to-apply/) 
 If you own a business 
 There are two places to sign up. Both are free. 
  1. SpaceX’s supplier page.  Go to spacex.com/supplier and choose “Become a Supplier.” SpaceX says it builds most of its own hardware but often uses “specialized, small, nimble, or local suppliers.” 
  2. The state’s Source Louisiana directory.  Louisiana Economic Development says SpaceX has joined Source Louisiana, which it describes as a pathway for Louisiana suppliers, contractors and service providers to compete for work on the project. Register at louisiana.supplierone.co. The state lists three steps: 
  Create a free business profile.  List what your company can do, plus its certifications and services.  Your profile becomes visible to major projects and their buyers.  
 The state says more than 4,000 Louisiana suppliers and contractors are in the directory. It also says plainly that signing up is no guarantee of work. 
 A training program for contractors 
 The state also runs a six-month program that gets small and mid-sized companies ready to bid on big-project work. The first class, 85 graduates, was honored last week. The state says companies can sign up now to be told when applications for the 2027 class open in January. 
 The numbers behind it 
 The state’s page on the project says SpaceX is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs over 10 years at an average salary of $92,600, and estimates another 8,100 jobs for local contractors and vendors. 
 It costs nothing to send a resume or register a business. Be careful with anyone who asks for money to get you hired. 
  Hiring in or near Vermilion Parish?  [Send us the opening](/send-news/) and we will check it and report it.

t: New Order Tells Every Federal Contractor to Alert the White House Before Answering Congress
d: Companies that work for the federal government, and their subcontractors, must report requests from Congress and follow White House instructions on what to hold back. Breaking the rule could cost a company its contracts.
b:
President Donald Trump signed an order dated Friday that puts a new rule on every company that does work for the federal government. 
 If Congress asks a contractor about its work or its communications with the executive branch, the company must tell the White House and the agency it works for right away. It must then follow any instructions it gets about holding back material the White House or the agency decides is covered by executive privilege. 
 The order is Executive Order 14438. It says contractors must do this “immediately.” 
 Who it covers 
   Every federal contractor.  The order does not limit the rule to defense or security work. A company that builds, hauls, supplies or does engineering under a federal contract is covered.   Subcontractors too.  The order says it applies to subcontractors working on a federal contract, and it makes the main contractor responsible for seeing that they follow it.   Requests already pending , and any that come later.  
 What happens if a company doesn’t 
 Agencies are told to consider “all appropriate actions,” and the order names three: ending or canceling the company’s contracts, suspending the company, or barring it from future federal work. 
 Why the White House says it is needed 
 The order says the executive branch has to be able to share sensitive information with contractors without it being passed on, “including to members of the Congress.” It says some congressional leaders have threatened to seek confidential information and have been “harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government.” 
 It also argues that when a contractor and the government answer the same request separately, the result is wasted effort and money. 
 What it does not settle 
 The order says it is to be carried out “consistent with applicable law.” It does not say how it fits with a company’s legal duty to answer a subpoena from Congress, and the text does not mention subpoenas. An executive order does not need a vote in Congress. 
 The White House budget office is told to write guidance for agencies on how to check that contractors are complying. Agencies are told to notify their contractors and subcontractors promptly.

t: Louisiana Is Adding Construction Jobs Faster Than Any Other State: 17,600 in One Year
d: Federal numbers for October show construction work here up 13% from a year ago. No other state is close. The Lafayette area, which includes Vermilion Parish, added about 1,400.
b:
Louisiana had 153,400 construction jobs in October. A year earlier it had 135,800. 
 That is 17,600 more people working construction in this state in one year, a 13% jump, according to federal jobs numbers. The Vermilion Times compared the same numbers for every state. No other state grew nearly that fast. 
 How Louisiana compares 
   Louisiana: up 13%.    Next closest, Iowa: up 8.4%.    The whole country: up 1.5%.  The nation added about 124,000 construction jobs in the year. About one of every seven was in Louisiana.  
 Only two states added more construction jobs by count, and both are far bigger: Texas, with 26,900, and Ohio, with 18,000. 
 Construction is carrying the state 
 Louisiana as a whole added about 40,000 jobs of all kinds in the year. More than four of every 10 were in construction. 
 Construction work here is close to its highest level on record. The peak, in numbers that go back to 1990, was 154,600 jobs in June 2018. September’s count of 153,800 was the second highest ever. October slipped by 400. 
 Closer to home 
 The federal numbers do not break out Vermilion Parish by itself. They count it as part of the Lafayette metro area. 
   Construction jobs in the Lafayette area:  about 12,400 in October, up from 11,000 a year earlier. That is roughly 1,400 more, also a 13% gain.   All jobs in the Lafayette area:  190,700, up 2,400 from a year earlier.  
 What the numbers don’t say 
 They do not say which projects are doing the hiring, what the jobs pay, or how many of the workers live here. The October figures are preliminary and can be revised. 
 A business group’s report on Nov. 17 said Louisiana will need nearly 42,000 new construction workers by 2028, and that the Lafayette region is one of three that could come up far short. [We covered that here.](/news/louisiana-42000-construction-workers-2028-lafayette-starbase/) 
 SpaceX has not posted any craft jobs for Pecan Island yet. [Here is every job it has posted and how to apply.](/news/every-spacex-job-open-pecan-island-12-positions-how-to-apply/) 
  How we counted:  We compared seasonally adjusted construction jobs for October 2026 and October 2025 in each state. Five states (Delaware, Hawaii, Maryland, Nebraska and Tennessee) report construction together with mining and logging. None of those grew more than 6.4%.

t: Every SpaceX Job Open at Pecan Island Right Now: 12 Positions, What Each One Requires and How to Apply

b:

 Three things to know first: 
   No pay is listed  on any of the 12 postings.   No craft jobs are posted yet.  There are no openings for welders, electricians, equipment operators, pipefitters or laborers at Pecan Island on SpaceX’s board.  Safety jobs 
  Sr. Manager, Environmental Health & Safety  (posted Oct. 15) Bachelor’s degree, 10 or more years in safety and environmental programs and 5 or more years managing them. Must live in or move to the Pecan Island area.  Apply  
  Manager, Environmental Health & Safety  (posted Nov. 13) Bachelor’s degree, 5 or more years in safety and environmental programs and 3 or more years managing them. The job is listed at Pecan Island, though one line of the posting refers to the Cape Canaveral, Florida, area.  Apply  
 Environmental and permit jobs 
  Sr. Environmental Engineer  (posted Oct. 15) Bachelor’s degree and 5 or more years running environmental compliance programs. Must live in or move to the Pecan Island area.  Apply  
  Sr. Environmental Engineer, Wetlands & Regulatory Compliance  (posted Nov. 6) Bachelor’s degree and 5 or more years in environmental consulting, engineering or regulatory review. Starts in Texas and moves to Louisiana in early 2027.  Apply  
  Sr. Environmental Regulatory Engineer, Air Permitting  (posted Nov. 6) Environmental or chemical engineering degree and 7 or more years getting major air permits for power plants or industrial sites. Based at Starbase, Texas; Bastrop, Texas; or Pecan Island.  Apply  
 Communications 
  Communications Lead  (posted Nov. 2) Bachelor’s degree and 5 or more years in communications, events or content. On site at Pecan Island full time.  Apply  
 Who can apply 
 Every posting says that, under federal export rules, an applicant must be a U.S. citizen or national, a permanent resident with a green card, a refugee or an asylee, or be eligible for the required federal authorization.

t: Trump Signs Law Ending the Penny and Letting Stores Round Cash Totals to the Nearest Nickel
d: Your pennies are still good money. But when a store can’t make exact change, the new law says how it may round. Cards and checks are not affected.
b:
President Donald Trump on Friday signed a law that ends penny production and sets a national rule for what happens at the register when nobody has one. 
 The law is called the Common Cents Act. The White House announced the signing Friday. 
 What it means at the register 
 The rounding rule applies  only to cash , and only when exact change can’t be given. A business is allowed to round. It is not required to. 
 The rounding is done on the  total, with tax included , not on each item. It can also be done on the change you are owed. 
   Ends in 1 or 2 cents:  may be rounded down. $10.02 becomes $10.00.   Ends in 3 or 4 cents:  may be rounded up. $10.03 becomes $10.05.   Ends in 6 or 7 cents:  may be rounded down. $10.07 becomes $10.05.   Ends in 8 or 9 cents:  may be rounded up. $10.08 becomes $10.10.  
 One exception: a whole purchase of 1 or 2 cents may be rounded up to a nickel. 
 A business can also round in your favor any time it wants, the law says. 
 What does not change 
   Pennies are still legal money.  The law says every penny already made stays legal tender. Stores can keep taking them and giving them.   Cards, checks, gift cards, money orders and electronic payments are not rounded.  Those are still charged to the cent.   Paychecks.  If an employer pays a worker in cash and chooses to round, it has to round  up . The law says it does not excuse anyone from minimum wage or overtime rules.  
 The rest of the law 
   No more pennies for circulation.  The Treasury must stop making them for everyday use. It may still make them to sell to collectors.   A cheaper nickel.  The Treasury may make the nickel with a zinc core and a nickel outer layer, if testing shows that saves money and works in coin machines.   State and local rules.  A business that follows the federal rounding rule cannot be found in violation of a state or local law for doing so.   Reports.  The Federal Reserve has 90 days to publish a plan for taking penny orders and deposits at the coin terminals that serve its banks. The Treasury must report on how the change affects low-income communities, older people and people without bank accounts.   Other coins.  Before the Treasury stops making any other coin, it must give Congress 60 days’ notice and a plan.

t: Ochsner Says Hackers Got Into Two Employee Accounts and Downloaded Files That May Include Social Security Numbers and Health Information
d: The hospital system, which runs Ochsner Abrom Kaplan Memorial Hospital in Kaplan, began notifying people Thursday. It says patient care and its medical records system were not disrupted, and it is still working out whose information was taken.
b:
Ochsner Health says someone broke into two of its employees’ accounts in September and downloaded files that may contain patients’ names, Social Security numbers and health information. 
 The hospital system runs Ochsner Abrom Kaplan Memorial Hospital in Kaplan and Ochsner Lafayette General Medical Center in Lafayette. It posted a notice on its website and began contacting people on Thursday. 
 What Ochsner says happened 
   Sept. 18 to 21:  An outsider got into two employee user accounts. Files in one of the accounts were downloaded.   Oct. 1:  Ochsner learned of it, locked down the accounts and brought in an outside forensic firm, the notice says.   Nov. 18:  Its review first confirmed that specific information had been accessed.   Nov. 19:  Notifications began.  
 Ochsner says the break-in was limited to its Microsoft environment, the email and office software side of the organization. It says there was  no disruption to patient care , to its electronic health record system, Epic, or to the MyOchsner patient portal. 
 What may have been taken 
 The notice says the files vary from person to person and “may include names, demographic information, Social Security numbers, and health information.” 
 Ochsner has not said how many people are affected, or which of its hospitals and clinics they used. It says its review is still going on to determine the full scope. 
 What to do 
   Watch your mail.  Ochsner says it will mail letters to the people whose information was involved, with formal notice coming over the next few weeks.   Credit monitoring.  People whose Social Security numbers were involved will be offered one year of it at no charge.   Questions:  Ochsner has set up a phone line at  844-971-8661 , open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Central, except major holidays.  
 Be careful with anyone who contacts you claiming to be from Ochsner about this. The notice says letters are coming by mail. If a caller or an email asks for your Social Security number or a payment, hang up and call the number above. 
 Ochsner says it has added to its cybersecurity safeguards since the incident.

t: Kaplan Rolls 56-6 and Delcambre Wins Again: Both Parish Teams Reach the Quarterfinals
d: Kaplan routed Vidalia at home. Delcambre, the No. 25 seed, beat No. 9 Grand Lake 41-15 and now draws the top seed in its bracket.
b:
Vermilion Parish went 2-for-2 on Friday night, and neither game was close. 
 Kaplan 56, Vidalia 6 
  No. 4 Kaplan  opened its playoff run by burying  No. 13 Vidalia 56-6  at home in the regional round of Division III Non-Select, according to the Louisiana High School Athletic Association’s bracket. Kaplan had a first-round bye, so this was its first game of the postseason.

t: SpaceX Starts Hiring Security for Pecan Island
d: Two listings went up this week, one to install cameras and access systems and one for executive protection. Neither requires a college degree. SpaceX now lists 12 jobs at Pecan Island.
b:
SpaceX has started hiring security for its Vermilion Parish site. 
 Two security jobs based in  Pecan Island  appeared on the company’s careers board this week. They are the first security jobs the Times has seen listed for the Louisiana project. They bring the number of SpaceX jobs listed at Pecan Island to  12 . 
 The two jobs 
  Sr. Physical Security Hardware Specialist  (posted Nov. 17). This is the person who puts in and keeps up the security equipment: door access systems, security cameras and the video system behind them. SpaceX asks for a high school diploma or equivalent and at least five years working on security systems such as cameras, access control or alarms. The listing also calls for a valid driver’s license, the ability to lift 35 pounds and a background check that allows access to facilities on Defense Department installations. 
  Sr. Physical Security Specialist  (posted Nov. 18). This one is closer to a bodyguard and security team lead. The listing describes protecting senior company leaders, watching for surveillance, sizing up risks and handling security for large company events. SpaceX asks for a high school diploma or equivalent, at least eight years in the military, law enforcement, overseas security contracting or advanced corporate security, and two years of executive protection or emergency response team work. Travel on short notice, up to 30% of the time, is part of the job. 
 What else is listed at Pecan Island 
 The other 10 openings are for engineers and managers getting the site ready: construction project management and construction safety, land development, materials management, environmental engineering and permitting, environmental health and safety, and a communications lead to work with the surrounding communities. 
 The oldest of those listings dates to mid-September. Most were posted in October and November. 
 How to apply 
 Every listing is on SpaceX’s careers page, spacex.com/careers. Search for “Pecan Island.” SpaceX says applicants for these jobs must be U.S. citizens, permanent residents or otherwise eligible under federal export rules. 
 Applying, or know someone who got a call back? Tell us at news@thevermiliontimes.com.

t: Trump, Xi and Putin Sign a Four-Point Declaration: Nuclear Talks, More Fuel, U.N. Changes and a Warning to the International Criminal Court
d: The White House published the text from Thursday’s three-way summit in Shenzhen, China. It is short on specifics and sets no deadlines.
b:
The first summit ever held among the leaders of the United States, Russia and China ended Thursday with a one-page statement and four promises. 
 President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Shenzhen, China, and put their names to what the White House calls a “Declaration toward Peace.” The White House posted the text the same day. Here is what it says. 
 1. Talks on nuclear risk 
 The three leaders restated a line that American and Soviet leaders first used in the 1980s: that a nuclear war “cannot be won and must never be fought.” They said their countries will hold talks on lowering nuclear risks and on keeping nuclear weapons from spreading. 
 The declaration doesn’t say when those talks start, who will lead them or whether they would cover limits on the three countries’ own arsenals. 
 2. More fuel 
 The three countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products,” the declaration says, and they stressed the need for steady energy flows. Refined products are the fuels made from crude oil, such as gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. 
 There are no numbers or dates attached. 
 3. Changing the United Nations 
 All three hold permanent seats on the U.N. Security Council. They committed to reforming the U.N. so it can respond better to world problems and stick to its core job of keeping the peace. The text doesn’t describe what would change. 
 4. A message to international courts 
 The leaders said the consent of nations and the legal immunity of government officials are “of paramount importance,” and agreed that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies “must not abuse their jurisdiction.” 
 What it isn’t 
 The declaration is a statement of intent, not a treaty. It names no war, sets no deadlines and creates no new organization. It says the leaders had an in-depth exchange on the state of the world and committed to “strategic stability and international security.” 
 The Times previewed the summit earlier this week. [That story is here.](/news/trump-xi-putin-first-three-way-summit-shenzhen/)

t: We Asked Vermilion Parish’s Three Power Providers How They Guard the Grid From Cyberattacks. One Answered.
d: Entergy sent a short statement. The City of Abbeville said it couldn’t verify an answer in time. SLEMCO did not respond.
b:
After a week in which flights were grounded nationwide and bank apps and Apple’s App Store went down, we had a simple question: what about the lights? 
 So the Times asked the three organizations that deliver electricity in Vermilion Parish,  Entergy Louisiana , the  City of Abbeville  and  SLEMCO , how they protect their systems from cyberattacks, including attacks helped along by artificial intelligence. We sent written questions Monday and Tuesday, followed up Thursday, and set a final deadline of 9 a.m. Friday. 
 We told each one we were not asking for technical details that could help an attacker. 
 Entergy: a statement 
 Entergy answered Thursday with a statement emailed by Brandon Scardigli: 
 “Entergy has dedicated cyber and physical security teams, a critical infrastructure protection department and a nuclear cybersecurity team responsible for implementing, maintaining and monitoring regulatory requirements. We maintain our information security status through ongoing diligence, investment and continuous monitoring.” 
 The statement did not address the rest of what we asked: whether attempted attacks are increasing, whether the company uses AI tools on defense, how it tests changes before they go live, or what customers in Vermilion Parish should know. 
 City of Abbeville: not in time 
 Abbeville runs its own electric system. Cristian LeJeune, the city’s media and communications coordinator, wrote Thursday that he was not comfortable speaking about the system’s cybersecurity without first confirming the information was accurate, and that the staff who could confirm it had been tied up with other pressing matters. 
 “I do not anticipate being able to provide a verified statement in time for publication,” he wrote. 
 We told the city we’ll add its statement to this story when it is ready. 
 SLEMCO: no response 
 SLEMCO, the member-owned electric cooperative, did not respond by the deadline. An automatic reply from its communications director said she was out of the office until Nov. 23. We sent the request to the alternate contact named in that reply on Tuesday and followed up Thursday, and did not hear back. 
 What we asked 
 Each provider got the same basic questions: 
  How do you protect the system from cyberattacks, including AI-assisted ones?  Are attempted attacks increasing?  Do you use AI tools yourselves to defend the system?  How do you test software and equipment changes before they go live?  Who oversees your cybersecurity?  What should customers watch for, including scams?  
 What Washington is saying 
 The outages the White House addressed this week involved the FAA, banks and Microsoft, and officials said none of them was an attack. In a release Wednesday, the White House said it sees no sign of a coordinated cyberattack or a foreign government behind them. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton put the trouble down to a wave of repairs: organizations are taking systems down to patch and upgrade them, and “they’re not coming back as expected in all cases.” 
 “Our systems need upgrades. They need patching,” Clayton said. [Our report on that is here.](/news/white-house-outages-not-linked-not-cyberattack/) 
 We’ll keep asking, and we’ll update this story as answers come in.

t: Biscuit Sandwiches and Gravy Meals Sold From Break-Room Coolers in Louisiana Recalled Over Listeria Risk
d: The products went out through workplace break rooms, grab-and-go coolers and vending machines in Louisiana and six other states. No illnesses have been reported, the company says.
b:
If you grabbed a biscuit sandwich out of the cooler at work in the past month, check the label. 
 A Texas food maker has widened a recall of ready-to-eat biscuit products that were sold in Louisiana, because the biscuits in them may carry  Listeria , a germ that can cause serious illness. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration posted the company’s notice this week. 
 What’s recalled 
  Fresh & Ready Foods LLC  of Longview, Texas, says two products made at its Longview plant are affected: 
   Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich , 5.7 ounces, wrapped in clear plastic film. Item number  3100048 , with “Fresh Thru” dates from  11/12 to 11/22  on the front label.   Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy , 9.5 ounces, in a clear clamshell. Item number  90013 , with expiration dates from  11/12 to 11/18  on the front label.  
 Both were shipped to  Louisiana . The sandwich also went to Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas, and the gravy meal went to all of those except Alabama. 
 Where they were sold 
 Not on grocery shelves. The company says the products went out between  Oct. 15 and Nov. 11  through  workplace break rooms, grab-and-go coolers, chilled vending machines and micro-markets , the small self-checkout snack shops found in many workplaces. 
 Why 
 The problem started with the biscuits. Fresh & Ready says it used biscuits from another company, C.H. Guenther & Son, which has expanded its own recall over possible Listeria contamination. Fresh & Ready first recalled some of the sandwiches on Nov. 8 and added more products on Nov. 17. 
 The company says  no illnesses have been reported . 
 Who is most at risk 
 The notice says Listeria infections can be severe, even deadly, for small children, the frail and elderly, and people whose immune systems are weak. Otherwise healthy people can be sick for a few days with a high fever, a bad headache, stiffness, nausea, stomach pain and diarrhea. In pregnant women, an infection can cause miscarriage or stillbirth. 
 What to do 
   Don’t eat it.  Throw away any of the recalled products you still have.  For a  full refund  or questions, call Fresh & Ready Foods at  1-855-424-8390 , weekdays from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Central.  
 If your workplace has one of these coolers or vending machines, pass this along to whoever stocks it.

t: State Puts SpaceX’s Wharf and Road Permit Out for Public Comment. Here’s How to Weigh In.
d: Louisiana’s coastal permit office marked the application complete this week and sent it out for review. The 25-day comment window opens with a legal notice set to run Saturday.
b:
The first big state permit for SpaceX’s Vermilion Parish project is now in front of the public. 
 Louisiana’s coastal permit office has put SpaceX’s application for a Gulf wharf, barge docks and a heavy-haul road near Pecan Island “on notice,” according to the state’s online permit tracker. That starts the clock on public comment. 
 How to comment 
 The Advocate, which is publishing the state’s legal notice, reports that the notice runs  Saturday, Nov. 21 , and that written comments will be taken for  25 days  from that date. By our count that runs through Dec. 16. 
 According to the notice as the newspaper describes it: 
  Send comments to the reviewer assigned to the case,  Melissa Sherman , at the Office of Permitting and Compliance,  P.O. Box 44487, Baton Rouge, LA 70804-4487 , or by email at melissa.sherman2@la.gov.  Put the permit number on it:  P20260831 .  Include your full name and contact information.  You can suggest changes, object and say why, or  ask for a public hearing .  
 Where the application stands 
 The state’s tracker lists the project as the “Southwest Louisiana Coastal Infrastructure Improvement Project” and shows this history: 
   Sept. 25:  SpaceX’s application arrives.   Oct. 1:  The state sends it back to the engineering firm that filed it as incomplete.   Nov. 9:  A revised application comes in.   Nov. 17:  The state marks it complete, assigns it to an analyst and sends it to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and the State Land Office.   Nov. 18:  It goes to The Advocate for the legal notice and to the Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, and the status changes to “On Notice.”   Nov. 19:  The Corps responds, and the application goes to the Department of Environmental Quality.  
 The tracker lists the application’s status as “Received - Under Review.” It does not show a decision or a hearing date. 
 What SpaceX is asking to build 
 As the Times reported from the application last week, the plan covers a Gulf-side wharf below the Freshwater Bayou lock, inland barge docks, canal dredging and a heavy-haul road of about 15.75 miles with a 1.5-mile bridge, with work running from 2027 to 2032. [Our earlier report has the details.](/news/spacex-permit-coastal-infrastructure-improvement-project-freshwater-bayou/) 
 The Advocate reports that the revised application filed this month says the wharf would let SpaceX ship Louisiana-made parts and equipment to its operations in Texas and Florida. The Times has not yet obtained that revised filing. 
 The federal side is separate. The Corps of Engineers reviews the same application under its own rules. 
 Do you live or fish near Freshwater Bayou? Tell us what you plan to say at news@thevermiliontimes.com.

t: White House: The FAA, Bank and Tech Outages Are Not Linked and Not a Cyberattack
d: The nation’s intelligence chief and Secretary of State Marco Rubio say the string of failures comes from companies and agencies patching and upgrading old systems.
b:
A nationwide ground stop. Bank apps that wouldn’t load. Apple’s App Store going dark. After a week of failures, a lot of people have been asking the same question: is somebody doing this? 
 The White House says no. 
 In a release Wednesday, the administration said it sees no sign of a coordinated cyberattack, a foreign government or any other bad actor behind the recent outages. It quoted the two officials who have been answering for it: Director of National Intelligence  Jay Clayton  and  Marco Rubio , the secretary of state and national security adviser. 
 “This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state,” Clayton said. 
 Not connected, they say 
 Rubio said the incidents have nothing to do with one another: “the Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago.” 
 “We are not under systemic attack,” he said. 
 So what is it? 
 Clayton’s explanation is that a great many companies and agencies are fixing security holes and replacing old equipment at the same moment, and some of that work is going badly. 
 Systems are being taken down, patched and upgraded, he said, and “they’re not coming back as expected in all cases.” Trouble also shows up where one system has to hand work off to another. 
 “Our systems need upgrades. They need patching,” Clayton said. 
 What we’ve reported 
 That account lines up with what the companies and agencies involved have said so far. 
  The FAA has said the Nov. 13 ground stop began with a router swap at a radio site in Arkansas and that it has no indication of a cyberattack. Its root-cause review is not finished. [Our report is here.](/news/faa-no-answer-louisiana-sites-ground-stop-router/)  Apple blamed Tuesday’s outage on an internal update and said it was not a cyberattack. [Our report is here.](/news/apple-outage-app-store-music-icloud-developers/)  
 The White House release is the administration’s own summary of its officials’ remarks. It did not publish technical findings on any of the outages.

t: Louisiana Will Need Nearly 42,000 Construction Workers by 2028, and the Lafayette Region Is Far Short, Report Says
d: A business group counted the workers needed to build 12 megaprojects, including SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana in Vermilion Parish. It says three regions, Lafayette among them, could come up about 19,000 workers short.
b:
The plants, data centers and launch pads Louisiana has been celebrating still have to be built, and a new report says the state doesn’t have nearly enough people to build them. 
 Leaders for a Better Louisiana, a statewide business and policy group, looked at 12 big industrial and technology projects announced over roughly the past year. Together they add up to about  $282 billion  in investment and about  7,550 permanent jobs , the group says. 
 Building them is another matter. At the peak, in  mid-2028 , the 12 projects alone could need  nearly 42,000 construction workers , which the group says is about half of all the industrial construction workers Louisiana has today. 
 Why it matters here 
  SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana , planned for the coast of Vermilion Parish, is one of the 12 projects, according to the project list published by 10/12 Industry Report. The others include LNG export plants near Lake Charles, Meta’s data center in north Louisiana and the Hyundai steel mill. 
 Better Louisiana says the squeeze will be worst in three regions:  Lafayette, Lake Charles and Monroe . Together they make up  81%  of the work at its peak, yet just  17%  of Louisiana’s industrial construction workers live there. Put every one of those local workers on these jobs, the group figures, and the three regions still come up  almost 19,000 people short . 
 It’s the skills, too 
 The group says the gap is not only a head count. Data centers need heating and cooling workers, LNG plants lean on pipefitters, and nearly every project needs electricians. Louisiana has stepped up training, it says, but there are still gaps in several high-skill trades. 
 Not a short boom 
 The peak comes in the next year or so, but the work doesn’t stop there. Better Louisiana estimates the 12 projects will keep  upward of 20,000  construction workers on the job for the next decade or longer. 10/12 Industry Report, citing the full report, says that long tail is driven largely by Starbase Louisiana and runs through early 2041. 
 The group’s chief executive, Adam Knapp, said in a statement reported by 10/12 Industry Report that “Louisiana has an extraordinary opportunity ahead,” and that the state needs more skilled workers and closer ties between employers and training programs. 
 Are you in the trades, or hiring? Tell us what you’re seeing at news@thevermiliontimes.com.

t: Democrat Mary Peltola Unseats Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan, State’s Count Shows
d: With every precinct reporting, Alaska’s official tally gives Peltola just over 50% of first-choice votes, enough to win without a ranked-choice runoff count.
b:
Alaska has a new U.S. senator. Democrat  Mary Peltola  has beaten Republican incumbent  Dan Sullivan , according to results posted Tuesday evening by the Alaska Division of Elections. 
 With all 401 precincts counted, the state’s summary report shows: 
   Mary Peltola (D): 144,302 votes, 50.12%    Dan S. Sullivan (R): 131,844 votes, 45.80%   Gerald L. Heikes (R): 6,105 votes, 2.12%  Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.: 4,760 votes, 1.65%  Write-ins: 885 votes, 0.31%  
 The Associated Press called the race for Peltola. 
 Why 50% matters 
 Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, where voters can rank the candidates in order. If nobody gets more than half of the first-choice votes, the last-place candidate is dropped and those ballots move to the voters’ next choice, round by round. Peltola’s 50.12% clears that bar on first choices alone. 
 The margin was about 12,500 votes out of nearly 288,000 cast in the race. Turnout was 47.9% of Alaska’s 605,433 registered voters. 
 Who they are 
 Peltola served in the U.S. House from 2022 to 2025 and was the first Alaska Native elected to Congress. Sullivan has held the Senate seat since 2015. 
 The state labels the results unofficial until they are certified.

t: State Will Pay for Starlink Dishes at About 10,500 Louisiana Homes, Including a Couple Hundred in Vermilion Parish
d: Louisiana signed a broadband grant agreement with SpaceX’s Starlink in June. The state’s broadband chief says residents won’t pay for the equipment, and a new round of grants is opening now.
b:
Some of the hardest-to-reach homes in Louisiana are getting satellite internet with the dish paid for by the state, and a couple hundred of them are in Vermilion Parish. 
 The agreement 
 Louisiana signed a grant agreement with SpaceX’s Starlink on June 11 under the federal Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program, known as BEAD, according to ConnectLA, the state broadband office. The office said the deal covers  10,635 locations in more than 50 parishes . 
 Starlink is one piece of a much larger plan. The state has $1.355 billion in BEAD money and is spreading it across fiber, fixed wireless and satellite providers, with a goal of reaching every home and business by 2028. 
 Who pays for the dish 
 ConnectLA Executive Director  Veneeth Iyengar  told KLFY this week that the state, and not the resident, will pay for the hardware. 
 “We will pay for that piece of equipment, not the resident, once SpaceX is ready to roll out,” Iyengar told the station. KLFY reported that eligible households would pay $55 a month for service. 
 Iyengar also told KLFY that Vermilion Parish is on the list: “even in the island area, there are a couple of hundred locations” where the state is paying for a Starlink unit. 
 Why satellite there and fiber somewhere else? Iyengar said it comes down to which companies bid on which addresses. 
 A new round is opening 
 ConnectLA’s website says the state is  opening a new round of grants  and has posted an updated list of locations. The public has until  Jan. 2  to review the list and weigh in. Iyengar told KLFY the office expects to announce the results of that round in February. 
 The location map and the updated list are on ConnectLA’s program page at connect.la.gov/bead. 
 If you live down the bayou 
 The Times has not seen the list of Vermilion addresses or a rollout date for the parish. If you’ve been told your home is one of them, or you’ve been waiting years for a decent connection, tell us at news@thevermiliontimes.com.

t: We Asked if South Louisiana’s FAA Sites Have the Router Behind the Ground Stop. The FAA Hasn’t Answered.
d: The agency’s press office did not reply by our Tuesday deadline. Its contractor, L3Harris, sent a statement that doesn’t mention Louisiana. Here is what is on the record and what isn’t.
b:
Four days after one equipment change in Arkansas grounded every flight in the country, the Federal Aviation Administration still hasn’t said whether the radio and radar sites that serve south Louisiana use the same kind of router. 
 The Vermilion Times put that question to the FAA’s press office on Sunday, along with five others, and asked for an answer by 5 p.m. Tuesday. None came. The only thing the agency sent back was an automatic reply saying the press office is staffed on weekdays. 
 What we asked 
  Were any FAA sites in Louisiana among the routers the agency changed after the ground stop?  Were Houston Center, which handles high-altitude traffic over south Louisiana, or Lafayette’s approach controllers among the facilities that went unstable?  Is the fix permanent, or a patch until something else is done?  Has this kind of work been stopped or moved to overnight hours?  When will the cause be known, and will the findings be public?  Does the FAA have a photo of the El Dorado, Ark., radio site we can publish?  
 What the contractor said 
 L3Harris, the company that runs the FAA’s network and was working at the El Dorado site on Nov. 13, did answer. In a statement Monday, a company spokesperson said L3Harris is “supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop,” and that more than 70% of the planned move from old copper lines to fiber is finished. 
 The statement did not address whether any site serving Louisiana has the same router, or whether the company has changed when it does this work. 
 What the FAA has said in public 
 The agency’s own question-and-answer page on the ground stop does speak to two of our questions, without naming any state. 
   The routers.  The FAA says it turned off the suspect function on the routers where the trouble began, then did the same on “more than 60 other Juniper routers in the system, and we have paused installing them.” It doesn’t say where those routers are.   The timing.  The El Dorado work was done in the daytime because it was a routine job at a remote site. After Friday, the FAA says, “we will reevaluate when we do replacement/maintenance work.”   How far it spread.  Seventeen of the FAA’s 22 en route control centers went unstable, along with several approach control facilities. The page doesn’t list them.   The cause.  The FAA says it has no sign of a cyberattack, and that it and L3Harris are still looking for the root cause.  
 What that leaves open 
 Nobody has said on the record whether a router like the one in El Dorado sits at a site that serves Lafayette or the skies over Vermilion Parish, whether those sites were among the ones that faltered, or how long the pause on new installations will last. 
 We’ll update this story if the FAA answers. [Our first report on the ground stop is here.](/news/faa-ground-stop-el-dorado-arkansas-router/)

t: Police Jury Wednesday: 2027 Budget Vote, a Response to the SpaceX Tax Deal Lawsuit and an Emergency Fix for the Mosquito Plane
d: Jurors meet at 5:30 p.m. at the courthouse, first to adopt next year’s budget and then for their regular monthly meeting. The agenda was posted Tuesday afternoon.
b:
The Vermilion Parish Police Jury is set to adopt its 2027 budget Wednesday evening, then decide how to answer the lawsuit that seeks to undo the parish’s tax deal with SpaceX. 
 Both meetings are in the Police Jury meeting room on the second floor of the courthouse,  100 N. State St., Suite 200, Abbeville . The special budget meeting starts at  5:30 p.m. , and the regular meeting follows it. Each one opens with a chance for the public to speak on anything on the agenda. The parish posted the notice Tuesday afternoon. 
 The 2027 budget 
 The budget meeting has one piece of business: to “discuss, review and adopt the 2027 budget.” The agenda doesn’t give totals. 
 One budget-related number is on the regular agenda. Jurors will be asked to approve moving  $383,040.17  from the parish’s dedicated tax funds, such as the health unit, road districts and the Ward 8 cemetery fund, into the general fund to cover their share of administrative costs. The parish’s table puts the administrative salaries being split at  $499,986 . 
 The SpaceX lawsuit 
 Two items from the Courthouse/General Needs Committee deal with the suit filed by the Vermilion Citizens Coalition and residents Cheryl Choate, Rebecca C. Young and Dr. Robert J. Young III against the Police Jury and the parish’s Industrial Development Board: 
  letting the parish’s lawyer  respond to the lawsuit , and  letting the lawyer  put out a press release  about it.  
 The plaintiffs say the two bodies broke Louisiana’s Open Meetings Law in approving the Starbase Louisiana tax agreement, as the Times [reported Oct. 30](/news/residents-sue-to-void-spacex-tax-deal/). The Police Jury declined to comment when the suit was filed, WWNO reported at the time. 
 The mosquito plane 
 The same committee recommends approving an  emergency engine repair and purchase  for the parish’s mosquito plane. The agenda doesn’t list a cost. 
 Coast and flooding 
  A resolution letting the jury president sign the paperwork to build  Phase II of the North Shore of Vermilion Bay Shoreline Protection Project .  The final payment to Broussard Brothers Inc. for the  Schooner Bayou rehabilitation  project.  A recommendation to  hold off on updating the parish’s Coastal Master Plan  until jurors talk again with Royal Engineering.  Having Sellers & Associates start the parish’s application to FEMA’s 2026  Flood Mitigation Assistance  program.  Three items on the  Chenier Au Tigre gap closure  project, including a closed session on a possible lawsuit against Great Midwest Insurance Co. and steps toward agreements with insurers to get the project finished.  
 Also on the agenda 
  Signing on to the  Albertsons opioid settlement , and paying JEPCO Holdings LLC for recovery housing services under the parish’s opioid program.  A resolution backing  St. Tammany Parish  in its court fight over state rules that make parishes pay for state offices without giving them the money to do it. t: Sheriff’s Office: Langlinais Has Not Said RV Parks Are Banned, and He ‘Is Not Opposed’ to Them
d: Answering questions from the Times, the Sheriff’s Office also said it has no say over RV park permits. Those calls belong to local governing bodies, and Abbeville’s council takes up new RV parks tonight.
b:
Vermilion Parish Sheriff Eddie Langlinais has not said RV parks will be kept out of the parish, and he doesn’t oppose them, the Sheriff’s Office told The Vermilion Times on Tuesday. 
 “Sheriff Langlinais has not made any statements that RV parks will not be allowed in Vermilion Parish, and he is not opposed to RV parks,” Ashley Adams, the office’s public information officer, wrote in an email. 
 Why we asked 
 A claim that the sheriff had said there would be no RV parks in Vermilion Parish reached the Times this week. We could not confirm it, so we did not report it. We put the question to the Sheriff’s Office in writing on Tuesday, and Adams answered the same afternoon. 
 The sheriff doesn’t issue the permits 
 Adams also said the question isn’t the sheriff’s to decide. 
 “The Vermilion Parish Sheriff’s Office has no authority over the approval or permitting of RV parks,” she wrote. “Those decisions are handled by the appropriate local governing authorities.” 
 Asked whether the office has public safety concerns about RV parks or housing for workers as the parish grows, Adams said: “The Sheriff’s Office’s main concern is public safety, and we will continue to serve and protect all areas of Vermilion Parish as our communities grow.” 
 Where the rules are being written 
 Two local bodies have RV parks in front of them this fall. 
   The Police Jury  approved a parish RV ordinance on Oct. 21, on the condition that its lawyer first strike every mention of temporary housing other than RVs, according to the meeting’s draft minutes. The final text had not been posted on the parish website when the Times [reported that vote](/news/police-jury-rv-ordinance-fines-levee-district/).   The Abbeville City Council  has a discussion and possible vote on “the establishment of new RV/Campground Parks” on [tonight’s agenda](/news/abbeville-council-tonight-rv-parks-meadows-phase-ii/). The council meets at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 101 N. State St., and takes public comment before it votes.  
 The Times has also sent written questions about that agenda item to the City of Abbeville and will report what the council does.

t: Border Crossings Hit Lowest October Ever Recorded, Customs and Border Protection Says
d: CBP counted 27,890 encounters nationwide last month, the fewest it has ever logged to start a fiscal year. Border Patrol arrests at the southwest border fell to 8,288.
b:
Fewer people were stopped at America’s borders in October than in any October CBP has on record. 
 U.S. Customs and Border Protection said Monday that it logged  27,890 encounters nationwide  last month, the lowest number it has ever recorded to open a federal fiscal year, which starts Oct. 1. That was 7% below September and the fewest for any month since February, according to the agency. 
 By the numbers 
   8,288:  Border Patrol apprehensions along the southwest border in October, down 7% from September. CBP says that is 95% below the monthly average under the Biden administration and fewer than the agency recorded in five days in October 2024.   18 months:  how long CBP says it has gone with zero releases of migrants at the border.   44%:  the jump in combined drug seizures from September, by weight. Agents seized about 14,700 pounds of methamphetamine and more than 9,000 pounds of cocaine in October.   $391 billion:  imports CBP processed in October, with  $26 billion  in duties identified for collection.  
 “President Trump unleashed the full strength of DHS to secure the border and enforce the law,” Homeland Security Secretary  Markwayne Mullin  said in the release. “The results speak for themselves.” 
 CBP Commissioner  Rodney S. Scott  said the agency now knows “more about who and what is entering our homeland than at any time in our nation’s history.” 
 What “encounters” means 
 An encounter counts each time CBP stops someone: Border Patrol arrests between ports of entry, plus people turned away as inadmissible at ports of entry. The same person can be counted more than once. The agency’s full monthly numbers are posted on its public stats pages.

t: Wildlife Agent Shoots Man Who Pointed Gun at Him on Eunice Night-Hunting Call, State Police Say
d: Louisiana State Police detectives are investigating Saturday night’s shooting on Chataignier Street. The man was taken to a hospital; no agents were hurt.
b:
A Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries agent shot a man in Eunice on Saturday night after the man came out of a house with a gun and pointed it at the agent, according to Louisiana State Police. 
 It happened shortly after  8 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 15 , on  Chataignier Street  in Eunice, about 40 miles north of Abbeville. 
 Wildlife and Fisheries agents had gone to the home about a  night-hunting complaint , State Police said. When they got there, a man walked out of the house armed with a firearm and aimed it at one of the agents, according to the agency’s preliminary findings. An agent fired, hitting him. 
 The man was taken to a hospital for treatment. State Police did not release his name or his condition, and no charges have been announced.  No agents were injured.  
 At Wildlife and Fisheries’ request, detectives from the State Police  Criminal Investigations Division’s Breaux Bridge field office  are investigating. State Police called it an active investigation and said more information will come out later. 
  Have information?  State Police are asking anyone with information, photos or video to contact detectives. Anonymous tips can go through the State Police website’s online report form, or by phone to  1-800-434-8007 .

t: Trump, Xi and Putin Will Meet Together for the First Time Thursday in China
d: China’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the first-ever three-way summit of the U.S., Chinese and Russian leaders for Nov. 19 in Shenzhen. Washington says peace and denuclearization are on the table; Moscow says the agenda is still being written.
b:
The leaders of the world’s three biggest nuclear powers are about to sit at the same table for the first time. 
 China’s Foreign Ministry announced Monday that President  Xi Jinping  will host President  Donald Trump  and Russian President  Vladimir Putin  for a  China-Russia-U.S. summit on Thursday, Nov. 19, in Shenzhen , the southern Chinese tech city hosting this year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings. Shenzhen is 14 hours ahead of Louisiana. 
 The three governments describe it as the first summit of its kind. The Kremlin calls it the “first-ever meeting in such a format.” 
 What each side says it wants 
  Washington:  In a Nov. 11 call, Secretary of State  Marco Rubio  and Chinese Foreign Minister  Wang Yi  talked about Trump’s trip to the summit in China and Xi’s planned visit to Florida for the G20. According to the State Department’s readout, the two agreed that leader-to-leader talks matter for goals “such as peace and denuclearization,” including at a possible three-way meeting with Russia. 
  Moscow:  Putin’s foreign policy aide  Yury Ushakov  said both Russia and the U.S. “see great value” in the Shenzhen summit, but that work on what it will actually cover is still underway. “We hope that this first-ever meeting in such a format will have a stabilising effect on the overall international situation,” he said. Ushakov also said Putin and Trump plan their own meeting on the sidelines, where the war in Ukraine will come up. 
  Beijing:  The Foreign Ministry’s announcement confirmed the date, the city and the three leaders, and little else. 
 Why it matters at home 
 Between them, the U.S., Russia and China hold the great majority of the world’s nuclear weapons. Any deal on arms, on Ukraine, or on trade between the three would reach far beyond Shenzhen, including the export markets Louisiana’s ports and farmers depend on. 
 The Times will report what comes out of Thursday’s meeting.

t: Four Seconds Short: Texas Beats LSU 22-21 on Last-Gasp Touchdown in Death Valley
d: The Tigers led most of the night behind two interceptions from safety Ty Benefield, but Arch Manning hit Raleek Brown from 4 yards out with four seconds left. LSU is 6-4 and heads to Tennessee on Saturday.
b:
LSU had Texas beat for almost the whole night. Then the clock showed four seconds. 
 On Saturday in Tiger Stadium, Texas quarterback  Arch Manning  threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to  Raleek Brown  with four seconds left, and the No. 6 Longhorns escaped Death Valley with a  22-21  win, according to LSU Athletics. It was the Tigers’ home finale. 
 How LSU built the lead 
 Texas scored first on a Manning 1-yard run. LSU answered right away: quarterback  Sam Leavitt  hit receiver  Jackson Harris  for a 10-yard touchdown to finish a 13-play, 75-yard drive. 
 Then safety  Ty Benefield  took over. He picked off Manning and ran it back 33 yards to the Texas 7, and Leavitt and Harris connected for a second score, this one from 9 yards, to put LSU up 14-7. LSU led 14-10 at the half after a missed 38-yard field goal. 
 Benefield intercepted Manning a second time in the third quarter, and running back  Dilin Jones  broke loose for a  44-yard touchdown run  to make it 21-10. 
 How it slipped away 
 Texas kicker  Gianni Spetic  chipped away with field goals of 41 and 50 yards, the first set up when LSU defensive end  Princewill Umanmielen  sacked Manning. The lead was down to five, 21-16, early in the fourth quarter. LSU’s offense didn’t score again, and Manning’s late strike to Brown won it. 
 Benefield’s line: two picks, a sack and eight tackles. Umanmielen also had eight tackles. 
 What’s next 
 The loss is LSU’s second straight, after a 31-13 defeat to Alabama the week before. Lane Kiffin’s Tigers are  6-4  overall and  3-4  in the SEC. 
 LSU finishes the regular season on the road: at  Tennessee  on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 2:30 p.m. Central, then at  Arkansas  on Nov. 28.

t: One Equipment Swap in Arkansas Shut Down America’s Skies. It Happened 225 Miles From Abbeville.
d: A routine change-out of network gear at a remote FAA radio site in El Dorado, Ark., flooded the nation’s air traffic system Friday. Every flight in the country was held on the ground, and the fallout stretched into Sunday.
b:
It wasn’t a hurricane. It wasn’t a hacker. It was one piece of equipment being swapped out at a quiet radio site in south Arkansas. 
 On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration says, new network gear installed at its  radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas , helped set off a flood of data that knocked the country’s air traffic system off its feet. Within hours,  every flight in the United States was held on the ground.  Thousands of planes already in the sky were brought down. Airports from coast to coast filled with stranded travelers, and the cancellations kept coming through Saturday and into Sunday. 
 El Dorado is about  225 miles north of Abbeville  as the crow flies. That’s roughly a five-hour drive up U.S. 167, just over the Louisiana line. 
 How one box took down the grid 
 The FAA’s contractor, L3Harris, was at the El Dorado site Friday installing a  new router , the box that moves data between the radio site and the rest of the FAA’s network. Transportation Secretary  Sean Duffy  said on CBS’s “Face the Nation” Sunday that the phone company was retiring the site’s old copper line, which forced a switch to fiber. “We brought in our routers and did the work, and that’s when we saw the flooding of the network,” he said. 
 At about  2:30 p.m. Central , the FAA’s network was hit with  a thousand connection requests every few seconds , according to the agency. A second site, a radar facility in  Amarillo, Texas , is also under investigation. The aging equipment on the other end couldn’t take it. Radio and radar feeds began failing at  17 of the 22  big control centers that guide planes between airports. 
 The FAA called a  nationwide ground stop . Roughly  3,500 planes  in the air at the time landed safely, the agency says. Flights didn’t start moving again until about  7:15 p.m. Central , nearly five hours later. The Philadelphia Inquirer reported it was the longest stoppage of its kind in 25 years. 
 Two days of chaos 
 Airlines canceled about  12,462 flights  on Friday alone, the FAA says. With planes and crews stuck in the wrong cities, the mess rolled into the weekend. In Philadelphia, more than 150 flights were canceled by Saturday afternoon, and dozens more were still being scrubbed on Sunday. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters that flying should recover fully by Sunday night, though he warned of more delays first. 
 Duffy said the same kind of switch has been made “thousands of times” without trouble, which is why crews at a remote site like El Dorado did the work in daylight. “We’re going to have to reevaluate now when we do this work,” he said. 
 What’s next 
 The FAA says there is  no evidence of a cyberattack . As a precaution, it shut off the same function on about  60 similar routers  across the country. The FAA and L3Harris are still hunting for the root cause, and Duffy said the FBI is helping. 
 Duffy called the system a 1980s network running on copper wire. He is asking Congress for  $50 billion  to rebuild it. 
 Are south Louisiana’s sites safe now? We asked. 
 The FAA hasn’t said where those 60 routers are, or whether any of them serve south Louisiana, where Houston Center handles most of the high-altitude traffic and Lafayette’s controllers handle the approaches. 
 So The Vermilion Times asked. On Sunday we sent questions to the  FAA press office  and to  L3Harris , the contractor that runs the network. We asked whether any Louisiana radio or radar sites have the same kind of router, whether shutting off that function is a permanent fix, and whether this kind of work has been paused or moved to overnight hours. We’ll report what they tell us, and when they don’t answer.

t: Louisiana’s Sen. Cassidy Calls RFK Jr.’s Tenure a ‘Series of Failures’ as the U.S. Loses Its Measles-Free Status
d: On national TV Sunday, the doctor-turned-senator urged parents to vaccinate, said he hasn’t decided how he’ll vote on Trump’s FDA pick Wednesday, and blamed a Democrat for stalling his Social Security plan.
b:
Louisiana’s senior senator went on national television Sunday and didn’t hold back on Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 
 Sen.  Bill Cassidy , a Republican and a physician who chairs the Senate health committee, told CBS’s “Face the Nation” that Kennedy is “obviously trying to provide cover for failure” at the Department of Health and Human Services. 
 Host Margaret Brennan opened the interview by citing a KFF report that measles is officially no longer considered eliminated in the United States. 
 “You could be the person that brings death to another” 
 Cassidy’s message to parents was blunt. Infants can’t be vaccinated against measles until around their first birthday, so they rely on everyone around them having had the shot. 
 “If you’ve not been vaccinated, you could be the person that brings death to another,” he said. “We’re seeing children die from measles who are too young to be vaccinated.” 
 He said that message should be “pounded, pounded, pounded,” and that if he were president, he would pick a new health secretary. He listed rising health costs, measles deaths, the lost elimination status and little progress on ultra-processed foods. 
 Brennan played a clip of Kennedy saying “the Senate no longer has any leverage over me” now that Democrats will control the chamber. Cassidy called that “a series of failures” being covered up. 
 Undecided on the FDA pick 
 Cassidy said he still doesn’t know how his committee will vote  Wednesday  on Dr. Heidi Overton, President Trump’s nominee for FDA commissioner. “I’ve been working the phones all week,” he said. “I cannot tell you the outcome of that vote right now.” 
 Social Security stalled 
 Cassidy also said he has commitments from Senate leaders and the president to move a bipartisan Social Security bill, but he blamed Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, for refusing to take part. His own plan would borrow $1.5 trillion and invest it in a fund separate from the Social Security trust fund to grow over decades. 
 “This is so important to our country,” Cassidy said. “Congress is there to take tough choices, and now those tough choices are being ducked.” 
 What do you think, should parents be doing more to protect babies from measles? Tell us in the comments.

t: Tanker’s Rudder Jammed Two Minutes Before It Rammed a Docked Riverboat in New Orleans, NTSB Says
d: Federal investigators say the Atlantic Asphalt’s steering failed as it passed under the Crescent City Connection Friday, sending it into the American Heritage. Everyone aboard the riverboat was accounted for.
b:
The tanker that slammed into a docked riverboat in New Orleans on Friday lost its steering about two minutes before the crash, federal investigators said Sunday. 
 The  Atlantic Asphalt , an asphalt tanker heading upriver, had just passed under the  Crescent City Connection  at about 12:26 p.m. on Nov. 13 when it suffered what the National Transportation Safety Board called a “steering casualty.” Its rudder was stuck turned to starboard, and the ship swung toward the river’s east bank, NTSB investigator-in-charge  Bart Barnum  said at a briefing. 
 At about 12:28 p.m., it hit the  American Heritage , an American Cruise Lines paddlewheel riverboat tied up near the Port of New Orleans. Everyone aboard the riverboat was accounted for. 
 Two minutes on the recorder 
 Investigators have more than nine hours of recordings from the ship’s “black box,” its voyage data recorder, which logs bridge audio, rudder angle, engine data, speed and heading, Barnum said. In those final two minutes, the audio picks up the ship’s whistle, radio warnings and calls for help, orders to drop the anchors and emergency maneuvering commands. 
 Investigators don’t yet know why the steering failed. They began interviewing the riverboat’s crew Sunday and plan to talk to the tanker’s crew starting Monday. 
 “We are investigating the personnel involved, the ships involved, and the environment at the time,” NTSB board member  John DeLeeuw  said. He said investigators will also study “the things that went right,” since no one was killed. 
 What’s next 
 The NTSB expects a preliminary report in about 30 days and wants to hear from anyone who saw the crash or caught it on camera. 
 The crash matters well beyond New Orleans. The lower Mississippi is one of the busiest shipping lanes in the country, and traffic on that stretch of the river was halted after the collision.
